issues.legal_issue: Amendments to a protected agrarian-reform scheme remain shielded from fundamental-rights challenge when they preserve the scheme and satisfy the conditions for that protection.
material_facts: The underlying tenancy legislation had previously been held to implement agrarian reform and to be protected from challenges under the fundamental-rights provisions.

The challenged amendments changed the procedures for recovering the purchase price from tenant-purchasers, allowed additional time in specified circumstances, and postponed the ineffectiveness of a purchase until recovery efforts failed.
The amendments retained the scheme under which tenants could acquire the land and former landlords could recover the purchase price.
The petitioner argued that the changes made recovery of the price and repossession of the land illusory or unreasonably delayed.
issues.conclusion: The amendments did not take the legislation outside the constitutional protection for agrarian reform. The petitioner could not challenge them under the fundamental-rights provisions, and the petition was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Under Article 31A, once legislation concerning agrarian reform is protected, an amendment changing details of its scheme is also protected if it does not take the legislation outside Article 31A or independently fall outside that protection, and the amending statute has received the President's assent. Changes to the transfer of tenure, payment by instalments, or postponement of payment do not alone remove that protection if the amendment continues to implement agrarian reform. Relying on Sri Ram Ram Narain Medhi v. State of Bombay, [1959] 1 Supp. S.C.R. 489, the Court treated the underlying legislation as protected; it held Maharana Shri Jayvantsinghji Ranmalsinghji v. State of Gujarat, [1966] Supp. S.C.R. 411, inapplicable. Once Article 31A applies, challenges under Articles 14, 19 and 31 cannot be pursued against the protected scheme.

rule.if: constitutional_challenge and underlying_agrarian_scheme_protected and amendment_preserves_agrarian_reform and presidential_assent

predicates.constitutional_challenge: A claimant brings a constitutional proceeding challenging the validity of legislation.
predicates.underlying_agrarian_scheme_protected: A prior ruling has treated the underlying agrarian-reform scheme as constitutionally protected.
predicates.amendment_preserves_agrarian_reform: The legislature changes details of the scheme while retaining its agrarian-reform purpose and operation.
predicates.presidential_assent: The amending legislation receives the President's assent.

issues.definition: When a constitutional challenge concerns an amendment to an already protected agrarian-reform scheme, the amendment preserves that reform, and the amending legislation receives presidential assent, the amendment is protected from fundamental-rights challenge.
